incidente.resumo: A software bug introduced by a Fastly deployment on May 12 was triggered on June 8 by a valid customer configuration change, causing 85% of Fastly's network to return errors in a global outage. Fastly identified and disabled the customer configuration; within 49 minutes 95% of the network was operating as normal, and a permanent bug fix began deploying later that day.

descricao.texto: The global disruption began at 09:47 UTC and was identified by Fastly monitoring at 09:48 UTC.
trechos: **09:48** Global disruption identified by Fastly monitoring

gatilho.texto: Early on June 8, a customer pushed a valid configuration change that included the specific circumstances that triggered the bug.
trechos: Early June 8, a customer pushed a valid configuration change that included the specific circumstances that triggered the bug, which caused 85% of our network to return errors.

descricao.texto: A software bug, introduced by a deployment that began on May 12, that could be triggered by a specific customer configuration under specific circumstances; the text does not describe the bug's mechanism.
trechos: On May 12, we began a software deployment that introduced a bug that could be triggered by a specific customer configuration under specific circumstances.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The bug was not detected during Fastly's software quality assurance and testing processes; why is still to be determined.
trechos: We’ll figure out why we didn’t detect the bug during our software quality assurance and testing processes.

descricao.texto: A software deployment begun on May 12 introduced the bug, which surfaced when a customer pushed a valid configuration change; neither the code change nor the configuration is named.
trechos: On May 12, we began a software deployment that introduced a bug that could be triggered by a specific customer configuration under specific circumstances.
Early June 8, a customer pushed a valid configuration change that included the specific circumstances that triggered the bug, which caused 85% of our network to return errors.

passos.texto: Fastly disabled the customer configuration (identified at 10:27 UTC); impacted services began to recover at 10:36 UTC, the majority had recovered by 11:00 UTC, and the incident was mitigated at 12:35 UTC.
trechos: We detected the disruption within one minute, then identified and isolated the cause, and disabled the configuration.
**10:27** Fastly Engineering identified the customer configuration

acoes.texto: Already done: a permanent fix for the bug was created and its deployment began at 17:25 UTC; it is being deployed across the network.
trechos: We created a permanent fix for the bug and began deploying it at 17:25.
We’re deploying the bug fix across our network as quickly and safely as possible.

acoes.texto: In progress: a complete post mortem of the processes and practices followed during the incident. Planned: finding out why the bug was not caught in QA and testing, and evaluating ways to improve remediation time.
trechos: We are conducting a complete post mortem of the processes and practices we followed during this incident.
We’ll figure out why we didn’t detect the bug during our software quality assurance and testing processes.
We’ll evaluate ways to improve our remediation time.

acoes.texto: Longer term: fully leveraging the isolation capabilities of WebAssembly and Compute@Edge to build greater resiliency.
trechos: Broadly, this means fully leveraging the isolation capabilities of WebAssembly and Compute@Edge to build greater resiliency from the ground up.
Within 49 minutes, 95% of our network was operating as normal.

perguntas_em_aberto: Why the bug was not detected during Fastly's software quality assurance and testing processes.

observacoes: The text gives no year for the incident (only "June 8" and "May 12"). duracao uses the stated 49 minutes to 95% of the network operating normally (onset 09:47 UTC, recovery began 10:36 UTC); the timeline also says the majority of services recovered at 11:00 UTC and the incident was mitigated at 12:35 UTC.
